Ethnicity, Social Dominance Orientation, Social Distance, Gender Role Attitudes, and Social Desirability all predict attitudes towards both the Indigenous group and the super-ordinate group in Guatemala.
similar ethnicity, close social proximity and egalitarian gender attitudes predict positive ethnic attitudes in Guatemala.
ethnic identity, SDO, gender roles and social desiribility are important factors to take into account when studying attitudes toward ethnic groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding ethnic attitudes and how they are affected by individual and social variables in a country with a long history of inter-ethnic conflict, Guatemala.
the influence of social and individual variables on inter-ethnic attitudes in Guatemala.
understanding the nature of ethnic attitudes, which are a central aspect of inter-group relations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

ethnic identity, social distance, social desirability, gender role attitudes as well as social dominance orientation are all factors that influence attitudes toward the Indigenous and Ladino group in Guatemala.
ethnicity is the main variable influencing ethnic attitudes in Guatemala.
ethnic attitudes are influenced by social variables (such as ethnicity and social distance) and individual variables (such as SDO, social desirability, gender role attitudes).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
social desirability is an important factor to consider when measuring ethnic attitudes.
ethnic attitudes are a consequence of both social group membership and individual difference characteristics.
social identity theory and social dominance theory are complementary, and that social identity theory is a necessary, but not sufficient, explanation for ethnic relations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ethnic attitudes in Guatemala are not just the result of social identities but also the product of individual difference characteristics.

ethnic attitudes may not be as simple as they seem, and that they may be a consequence, not only of group memberships but also of individual difference variables such as social dominance orientation and social desiribility.
the relationship between ethnic identity and ethnic attitudes is complex and is not a one-way street.
